nodes.summary: Algebraic core of Cochran's theorem for `Q`: if `Xᵢ = θ + √vᵢ zᵢ` with `vᵢ > 0`, then `Q` is the squared distance from `z` to the line spanned by `a = (vᵢ^{-1/2})ᵢ`, i.e. the squared norm of the projection of `z` onto the orthogonal complement of that line.
nodes.title: Cochran's Q as a squared projection norm

nodes.summary: Cochran's heterogeneity statistic `Q = ∑ᵢ vᵢ⁻¹ (Xᵢ - ∑ⱼ wⱼ Xⱼ)²` of the estimates `X` with variances `v`, where `w = inverseVarianceWeights v`.
nodes.title: Cochran's heterogeneity statistic Q

nodes.summary: Fisher's combined statistic `-2 ∑ log pᵢ` of `k` p-values.
nodes.title: Fisher's combined statistic

nodes.summary: For `k ≥ 2` independent Gaussian estimates `Xᵢ ~ N(θ, vᵢ)` with positive known variances, Cochran's `Q` has the chi-square law with `k - 1` degrees of freedom.
nodes.title: Cochran (1954)

nodes.summary: Fisher (1932), §21.1: for `k ≥ 1` independent p-values, each uniform on `[0, 1]`, Fisher's statistic `-2 ∑ log pᵢ` is chi-square with `2k` degrees of freedom.
nodes.title: Fisher's method for combining p-values

nodes.summary: `-2 log U` has the exponential law of rate `1/2`, i.e. chi-square with two degrees of freedom, when `U` is uniform on `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Minus twice the log of a uniform variable is chi-square

nodes.summary: Stouffer's method (Stouffer et al. 1949; Liptak 1958): for independent standard normal z-scores and a nonzero weight vector, the weighted z statistic is standard normal.
nodes.title: Stouffer's method

nodes.summary: Optimality of inverse-variance weighting: for positive variances `v` and weights `c` summing to one, `∑ cᵢ² vᵢ ≥ (∑ vᵢ⁻¹)⁻¹`. The gap is `∑ vᵢ (cᵢ - wᵢ)²` for the inverse-variance weights `w`.
nodes.title: Optimality of inverse-variance weights

nodes.summary: The inverse-variance (fixed-effect) weights `vᵢ⁻¹ / ∑ⱼ vⱼ⁻¹` for study variances `v`.
nodes.title: Inverse-variance weights

nodes.summary: Stouffer's weighted z statistic `∑ wᵢ zᵢ / √(∑ wᵢ²)` of the study z-scores `zᵢ`.
nodes.title: Stouffer's weighted z statistic

nodes.summary: The inverse-variance weights sum to one.
nodes.title: Inverse-variance weights sum to one

nodes.summary: The variance `∑ wᵢ² vᵢ` of the inverse-variance-weighted average is `(∑ vᵢ⁻¹)⁻¹`.
nodes.title: Variance of the inverse-variance-weighted average

nodes.summary: Cochran (1954): for pairwise independent square-integrable estimates `X i` with positive variances, the inverse-variance-weighted average has variance `(∑ Var[Xᵢ]⁻¹)⁻¹`, the smallest variance among all weighted averages `∑ cᵢ Xᵢ` with `∑ cᵢ = 1`.
nodes.title: Cochran's minimum-variance theorem for weighted averages

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
